headline: Speaker sends the House home early, skipping a vote
summary: Speaker Mike Johnson sent the House home a day early Wednesday so members can campaign for the midterms. Rep. Thomas Massie had filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war. Cancelling Thursday pushes any vote past the election. Massie says that was the point. Johnson calls his push a stunt.

cover_question.q: Why did they all go home early?

cover_answer: To campaign, says the speaker. To skip a vote, says Massie.
table_question: Is ending the game early fair if the rules let you?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The House is the big group in Washington that makes laws. Its leader sent everyone home a day early. One member, Thomas Massie, wanted a vote and said that was not fair, like a teacher ending class right before your turn to talk. The vote can wait. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Ending early before your turn is a fairness call they feel at once.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Rep. Thomas Massie wants a House vote on removing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Speaker Mike Johnson cancelled Thursday's session, and the vote now waits until after the election. Like a referee ending the game early: no whistle, no play.
8-12.why: Who controls the clock is a fairness fight they know.

13-17.script: Is it fair to end the session so a vote can't happen? Massie says Johnson cancelled Thursday to dodge his Hegseth impeachment vote. Johnson calls that ridiculous and the push a publicity stunt. Who should control the calendar?
13-17.why: Teens can weigh a legal move against a fair one.

5-7.q: Why did they all go home early?
5-7.a: The speaker said the work was done and it was time to campaign for the election. Another member said it was to skip a vote he wanted.

8-12.a: A House vote on formal charges against an official. Massie filed eight against Hegseth. No vote happened.

8-12.q: Can the speaker just do that?
8-12.a: Yes. The speaker sets the calendar. Massie says Johnson could have held the vote Wednesday.

13-17.a: Recessing for October in an election year is common. But by one tally the House has cut a net 24 days this year, about a fourth of its schedule.

13-17.q: Why does Massie care so much?
13-17.a: He says he is trying to stop a war and get justice for Epstein survivors. He lost his primary after Trump campaigned against him and leaves soon.
